changes.sprint: A simulation-time anaerobic reserve updates once per active player tick. Requested sprint spends it, rest/walking recovers it, and partial recovery is reusable. A smooth speed ceiling plus depleted-state hysteresis prevents per-frame sprint/jog oscillation. The human HUD displays the reserve and all 21 CPU players use the same implementation.
changes.walking: Light-stick slow control and movement copies bake a short overlapping-support gait on the native skeleton, with a 45 mm swing lift. The original lower-body pose is preserved around each ball-contact event, and transitions smoothly back to walking. Full-stick/RB source gait and original asset files remain unchanged.
changes.passing: A short tap starts from a useful 5 m/s floor with a progressive charge curve to 22.2 m/s. Real rendered trials measure separate tap/held responses.
changes.flight: Physical passes, crosses, shots, volleys and headers derive bounded angular impulse from actual weighted-skin contact position and delta velocity. Opposite side contacts yield opposite curve, high/low contacts distinguish top/backspin, and central firm kicks may enter the existing low-spin wake model. Native trajectory integration and prediction remain shared.
changes.balance: Stronger but bounded acceleration/cut counterbalance and dribbling torso/arm recruitment make weight shifts more visible. Actual aerial shoulder contacts amplify reciprocal support load; active balance and native protective steps still decide support recovery or falling.
changes.aerial: CPU contested-header preparation is eligible near goal unless another finishing action already takes priority. A rendered contested fixture verifies both participants select native jump-header motions, an actual head contact occurs, and real body-contact forces occur.
changes.keepers: The catch/parry criterion retains manageable arrivals only for authored retaining poses and real contact, while stronger arrivals require parrying. Parry direction uses ball/hand side to favor the side of the goal mouth. Existing timed dives and intentional backpass foot rules remain.
changes.tactics: CPU actors conserve reserve on non-urgent support runs, retaining native formation, defensive circulation, combinations, overlap and crossing choices.
changes.preparation: The bounded whole-player preparation-clearance planner also covers stationary foot kicks. It prevents a supporting shoe from kicking away a resting ball before the intended crossing strike, without turning off collisions, extending a limb or enlarging the skin tolerance.

investigated_findings: The first rendered walking test found that the selector repeatedly chose slow BallControl, so a Movement-only walking adaptation was not visible. The actual selected slow control clips now use the walking gait outside their protected native contact interval.

A stationary generated inside-foot cross struck the ball with the opposite supporting shoe during preparation and missed its intended later contact. The clearance planner found a 0.12 m whole-player support arc, improving minimum predicted clearance from penetration to 8.4 mm; the repeated rendered cross completes a real foot event.
The completed initial preflight recorded those two failures. Its older binary evidence is excluded from this release report; all selected final cases have the exact same fresh native executable hash.
limits: Rendered regressions use Linux/X11, a virtual Xbox controller and the OpenAL null driver. The Windows binary is cross-compiled and statically packaged/validated; Windows GUI execution, physical controller feel and audible balance still require the user PC.
This is a native animation-driven/Bullet prototype with constrained procedural responses, not Euphoria, GTA code, a learned motor policy or new captured animation data.
Friction, reserve and aerodynamic parameters are calibrated game approximations, not a proof of perfect real-world biomechanics or ball aerodynamics.

Keeper catch eligibility is unit checked. Rendered keeper fixtures verify foot receptions, attempts and body/hand deflections; they do not prove every feasible shot is held or every match situation is covered.

The approved controlled ground-dribble collision exemption remains. Existing real skin checks do not establish universal absence of interpenetration, and catalogue counts are compatible profiles rather than exhaustive visual validation.
